newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Korona to launch 2 new funds on Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Korona to launch 2 new funds on Jan 20.

text.p: Poland's mutual funds company Towarzystwo Korona said on Friday it would add on January 20 a new equities fund and a money market fund to a balanced fund it has been operating since August 1995.

"Our new funds are an important step in the company's strategy of increasing investors' access to...professional management of an ever broadening menu of investment tools," Korona's president David Glasgow told a news conference.
He said that during the first 11 months of 1996 the balanced fund's net assets grew more than 2.5 times to 49.3 million zlotys, while the unit's net asset value grew 60 percent.
Korona's chief strategist, Jeffrey Skipper, said that he expected the funds to show good results this year as he expected further gains on the Polish stock market. He did not give specific forecasts.

"Such developments as the listing of the National Investment Funds (NFIs) and large privatisations should improve foreign investors' opinion about the Polish market and their activity will result in good performance of the (Polish) shares," Skipper said.
Korona's analyst Tomasz Krysztofiak said the money market fund would include short-term debt instruments such as treasury bills and commercial papers of up to one year of maturity.
He said Korona would aim to outperform short-term banking deposits.
He also said that listed shares would make up more than 70 percent of the equities fund.

Korona is a joint-venture between Creditanstalt Securities SA, a Polish broking subsidiary of Austria's Creditanstalt -Bankverein, and of Polish state-owned agriculture bank Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA.
